fit.title: 1. Check every cell of the piece
fit.question: Place a horizontal two-cell piece. Which option fits without overlapping an occupied cell?
fit.reason: B2 is empty, but C2 is occupied. A piece needs room for every cell, not just its first cell. Placing at B1 and C1 completes row 1, which then clears under these exercise rules.

clear.title: 2. Look across and down
clear.question: Place a single-cell piece. Which option completes both a row and a column?
clear.answer: A completes row 1 and column C.
clear.reason: Both lines are full after placing at C1, so both clear together. Their shared cell belongs to both lines but is removed only once: seven occupied cells disappear, leaving this small board empty. B fits but completes neither line. This is a space calculation, not a scoring rule.

space.title: 3. Leave room for the next shape
space.question: Place the horizontal two-cell piece first, then a 2-by-2 square. Which first option leaves a legal place for the square after any completed lines clear?
space.answer: A leaves space for the square; B does not.
space.reason: A completes and clears row 3. You can then place the square at C1, D1, C2 and D2, among other positions. B clears nothing and breaks up the open area near the top. Eight cells remain empty after B, but none form a 2-by-2 square. Count usable shapes, not only empty cells.
